function: Joint source-channel coding of images over MIMO: ViT encoder learns symbol mapping and power allocation, a learned residual refines ZF equalization, ViT decoder reconstructs the image (pp. 5, 7).
system: MxM MIMO, 2x2 default (M=2-4; 32 in Fig. 10), open-loop CSIR and closed-loop CSIT, i.i.d. block complex Gaussian fading, no RIS, carrier frequency not stated (pp. 3, 8, 13).
method: ViT encoder-decoder with channel-heatmap input and learned ZF residual; end-to-end autoencoder training on MSE plus 0.1 LPIPS, per-SNR or random-SNR; no federated or meta-learning (pp. 6-9).
data_channel: CIFAR10 and ImageNet crops for training, Kodak and CelebA for testing; simulated i.i.d. complex Gaussian block fading plus AWGN; no 3GPP or measured channel (pp. 8, 9, 13).
test_conditions: Per-SNR or random-SNR [0,22] dB training; test 0-20 dB, R=1/24-1/6; ImageNet-trained, tested on Kodak/CelebA; M=2-4 antennas; imperfect CSI trained and tested (pp. 9-14).
baselines: Non-learned: BPG or VTM with LDPC and sphere decoding, BPG-Capacity. Learned: neural-codec compression (MBT2018, ELIC, Cheng2020) with LDPC or capacity; CNN and Swin DeepJSCC backbones (pp. 9, 11, 13).
metrics: PSNR, LPIPS; parameters, FLOPs, encoding and decoding time (pp. 4, 11).
complexity: Table IV (p. 11): 6.61-19.23 M parameters, 0.43-1.23 GFLOPs for Lt=4-12; O(4ld^2+2l^2d); 4.82/5.16 ms GPU encode/decode versus 37.25/71.28 ms for BPG-LDPC on CPU.
openness: none; no code or data link, only public image datasets (CIFAR10, ImageNet, Kodak, CelebA) (p. 8).
q1_support: p. 8: "Each element of H is sampled from a complex Gaussian" - custom i.i.d. Gaussian block-fading channel; the correlated channel is only in the appendix of [46]; no 3GPP, COST 2100, DeepMIMO or measured data.
q2_support: p. 9: "perform well on a never-seen dataset" - trained on ImageNet crops, tested on Kodak (CelebA on p. 13); the shift is in the image source, the channel stays i.i.d. Gaussian.
q3_support: p. 8: "BPG-LDPC schemes at different SNR values and bandwidth" (non-learned, PSNR); p. 11: "FLOP counts when achieving the best transmission" performance, Table IV PSNR at Lt=8: proposed 24.41, CNN-based 23.54, Swin-based 23.61 dB.
q4_support: p. 11: "operations by up to 44.74% and 61.4%, respectively" - Table IV gives parameters, FLOPs, order of complexity and encoding/decoding time.
q5_support: p. 8: "Our model was implemented in Pytorch with two GTX" 3090Ti GPUs - implementation described but no code or data link anywhere; datasets are images of the learning task and the channel is simulated.
notes: Borderline on rule 5 (JSCC counts only if the learned method also performs a listed function): included because the learned residual retrieves X' from Y after ZF (p. 7, area 1) and the encoder learns power allocation (p. 5, area 3); area 1 chosen since the main metric PSNR measures recovery at the receiver, area 3 is the alternative. q3 rests on Table IV, where the CNN and Swin entries are alternative backbones of the same scheme, so the reviewer may read them as variants. q2 rests on the image dataset shift only.
